contracts.action: Reconnect to a managed remote server that is alive but not answering now waits up to T3_READY_TIMEOUT_MS and then exits 1, instead of killing and relaunching after the 2s reuse probe
contracts.equivalent_path: The same branch before this change (kill -0 then a 2s wait_ready, then kill and relaunch), and the fresh-launch readiness wait at tunnel.ts:744
contracts.before_after: Before: 2s probe failed, server killed, new one launched. After: wait_ready with the 60s budget; on failure prints 'left running' to stderr and exits 1 without touching PID/port/managed files. A changed runner (RUNNER_CHANGED=1) still kills and replaces.
contracts.visible_effect: A temporarily busy server (long SQLite stall) now survives a reconnect. A server hung for good makes every reconnect fail after 60s with the stderr message, until the user disconnects.
contracts.failure_mode: The wait is bounded by one wait_ready call of 60s, inside the 90s node-mode launch timeout (REMOTE_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS) and the 900s archive timeout. Nothing else in this branch waits; wait_for_pid_exit is capped at 2s. disconnectEnvironment runs stopRemoteServer even without a tunnel entry (tunnel.ts:1771-1791), so a hung managed server can be stopped from the UI.

contracts.action: Stale SSH forward replacement now deletes the map entry before closing it, so the entry's scope finalizer skips the remote stop
contracts.equivalent_path: disconnectEnvironment deletes the entry and closes it (tunnel.ts:1782-1785), then runs the remote stop explicitly
contracts.before_after: Before: closing a stale entry ran the finalizer, which stopped the remote server (tunnels.get(key) === entry), so each stale forward restarted the remote. After: the finalizer sees stopRemote=false (tunnel.ts:1587-1599), kills only the local ssh process, and createTunnelEntry relaunches via the launch script, which reuses the running server.
contracts.visible_effect: A dropped forward reconnects without restarting the remote server or its agents.
contracts.failure_mode: If createTunnelEntry then fails, no entry exists and the remote stays running. This matches the intent, and disconnect still stops it. The readiness probe has a 2s overall timeout (tunnel.ts:1657), so the stale check is bounded.

contracts.action: Adoption of a default-home server no longer falls back to killing DEFAULT_RUNTIME_PID when no managed PID is recorded, and a later readiness probe is skipped while the adopted PID is alive
contracts.before_after: Before: a managed marker with no PID file made the script kill the external server it was adopting. After: only a recorded REMOTE_PID is killed. A runtime file naming our own managed PID is kept as ours. The second wait_ready is skipped when server_running ADOPTED_PID is true. The server_running check skips zombies (ps stat Z) and trusts kill -0 when ps gives nothing.
contracts.visible_effect: Reconnecting no longer kills a service-owned server or starts a second server on the same home after a momentary stall.
contracts.failure_mode: If the adopted server exits during the handover, server_running fails and the 2s reuse wait_ready falls through to a relaunch. This is bounded by that 2s probe plus wait_for_pid_exit (2s).

summary: I read both files in full and found no defects in this part. The launch-script changes in `packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts` match what the PR says they do. A managed server whose recorded PID matches the default runtime file is kept. The kill fallback to the default-home PID is gone. A zombie no longer counts as running. A live adopted server is not probed a second time. A stalled managed server now gets the 60s readiness wait and an exit 1 instead of a kill and relaunch. Deleting the tunnel map entry before closing a stale forward correctly stops the finalizer from stopping the remote server. Disconnect already uses the same delete-then-close order. The new tests run the real generated script against a fake server and cover each of those behaviours. The cost is a few real wall-clock waits, including a 5s sleep.
